evidence.note: Upfront the agent enumerates the full subsystem set (stdlib server, start.sh, static assets, durable SQLite storage, seed data, three pinned JS libs) and sequences foundations first: create static dir + vendor libs before building. A defensible dependency-aware order, but the entire app is then written in a single monolithic 'cat > /app/app.py' rather than incremental milestones.

The validation plan lists rough done-criteria across major subsystems — health, static hashes, UI pages, OAuth/token flows, API timelines/posting/actions, admin-scoped endpoints, seed counts — a checkable smoke-test set, but applied as one end-pass rather than per-milestone gates.

Compatibility gaps (remote-author seeding, OAuth authorize, trends/preferences/markers, favourited_by/reblogged_by) are discovered late and patched reactively, indicating subsystems weren't carved into discrete verified increments up front.

Wrap-up recaps subsystems validated (hashes, OAuth, introspection, admin, lists, idempotency, seed) confirming a rough coverage list existed, but no living/revised milestone hierarchy with explicit per-item done-checks driving each step.

reasoning: The agent had a sensible, foundations-first ordered plan covering the major subsystems (storage/static libs before validation) with a rough smoke-test checklist as done-criteria — squarely the level-5 anchor. It falls short of level 8 because there were no dependency-aware milestones each with an explicit verification hook gating the next; the app was written monolithically and validated in one late pass, with several subsystems (remote seeding, OAuth authorize, extra endpoints) surfaced and patched reactively rather than sequenced as de-risked increments.
